Subject: Need short-term GPU bridge ahead of Q1 expansion

Marissa / Redwood team,

Quick context: our product usage is spiking as we onboard two new enterprise customers in early Q1. We expect sustained 3x token throughput starting mid-Jan through Feb, with an unpredictable tail. Our renewal is scheduled for the end of November, but the ramp is earlier.

As it stands today we project a shortfall in steady-state capacity to meet SLA targets during the ramp window. Can Redwood provide a provisional "bridge" of GPUs for ~6 weeks (estimated 40 V100-equivalent slots) while we finalize the renewal and committed tranche?

Requirements:
- Low-latency paths maintained (p95 target)
- Temporary pricing or credit for the bridge period
- Clear handoff plan to convert any sustained usage into committed capacity before renewal closes

What we need from you: a feasibility note and rough cost/approval path by Friday so we can align with procurement and our execs.

Thanks,
Daniel Hsu
Head of Infra, HelixAI

Marissa — quick ops read: feasible. Notes below.

- Capacity: we can stage a 40 vGPU burst from our Dedicated burst pool. Equivalent to roughly 40 A10s/V100s depending on the shape you need. Lead time: ~3–5 business days for allocation and routing.
- Latency: with continuous batching and KV caching enabled, p95 should hold within current SLA +/- ~10–20ms in peak; p99 impact negligible if we pin hot paths. Will need a short maintenance window to seed caches.
- Conversion path: recommend 2-phase approach:
  1) Bridge (6 weeks) — use burst pool with strict prefix caching and limited max-timeout to conserve KV memory.
  2) If usage > 60% sustained for 7 days, convert X GPUs to a committed slab and re-provision the remainder back to burst.
- Risk: if Helix spike is highly spiky (sub-minute bursts), we'll need additional autoscale headroom which increases cost by ~12% due to pre-warming.

Estimated cost for 6-week bridge (back-of-envelope):
- Raw GPU hours: 40 GPUs * 24h * 42 days = 40,320 GPU-hours.
- List rate (burst pool): ~$0.65/GPU-hour => ~$26k gross.
- Suggested time-bound credit: 30–50% applied as an invoice credit or usage rebate during the bridge window.

I'll attach a small ops checklist to the SOW for network egress and KV warming tasks.

Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Folks — finance view and commercial options. TL;DR: we can offer a 40% credit on the incremental bridge portion with an acceleration clause tied to conversion. Details: 

Option A (preferred):
- 40 GPU bridge for 6 weeks, 40% usage credit applied to invoice for bridge period.
- If Helix converts at least 50% of the bridged capacity into a committed tranche at renewal, Redwood will apply a one-time additional credit equivalent to 10% of the committed tranche value (to be amortized over first billing cycle).

Option B (conservative):
- Standard burst pricing, with a 20% credit and no conversion bonus.

Notes:
- Any SLA exception that increases our operational exposure (explicit uptime/SLO guarantees beyond standard) requires VP approval — recommend we route to Aditya for sign-off.
- Need Procurement to confirm PO cadence; if they can issue a PO by Nov 15 we can align the committed tranche with our Q4 provisioning window.

Kimberly Park
